summary:
Found and fixed the needle: `InstallSnapshot` in `app/snapshot.go` set `lastApplied` from the snapshot but never touched `commitIndex`, and never compacted the log for the common case where the snapshot doesn't exceed the existing log.

This mattered specifically because `Restart()`'s recovery logic derives `lastApplied` from `commitIndex`. Since `InstallSnapshot` left `commitIndex` at its stale (0) value, a restart dragged `lastApplied` back down to 0 — while the uncompacted log still held entries 1–10. When the new leader later sent more entries, `applyEntries()` replayed 1–10 a second time on top of the already-restored snapshot state, doubling every key's apply count.

Fix (matches the two "omissions" the bug description alluded to):
1. `n.raftLog.CompactUpTo(snap.LastIncludedIndex)` when the snapshot doesn't exceed the log, so superseded entries are discarded.
2. `if snap.LastIncludedIndex > n.commitIndex { n.commitIndex = snap.LastIncludedIndex }` so commit state stays consistent with lastApplied across a restart.

**Verification:** `test.sh` hardcodes `go build -o /usr/local/bin/raft-snapshot`, and in this sandbox that path is root-owned (not writable by the `bench` user) — even with sandbox restrictions disabled, it's a real filesystem permission (uid 1001 vs root, mode 755), so `test.sh` itself can't run here. I built the binary directly (`go build -o /tmp/raft-snapshot .`) and ran the equivalent checks:

- `raft-snapshot check` → `PASS: All 13 keys present, no duplicate applies`
- `raft-snapshot simulate` trace confirms node3 only applies entries 11–13 after restart (not re-applying 1–10) → `PASS: No duplicate applies detected`

The scenario is fully deterministic (no randomness), so the 3-round loop in `test.sh` would pass identically each time.
